epics.title: M2: Execute captured workflows with the owned engine
epics.outcome: A developer can execute captured local workflow inputs and trust the reported terminal result.
epics.exit_evidence: RR-7 records end-to-end success, failure, captured-input isolation, cancellation and restart evidence; all M2 stories satisfy their acceptance criteria.

stories.title: Parse Actions YAML and produce deterministic capability-checked plans
stories.value: see whether a workflow is supported before any work launches
acceptance: Given bounded valid first-subset YAML, planning preserves on/string keys and emits the same canonical plan digest for identical inputs.
Given duplicate keys, malformed/oversized input, unsupported fields or expressions, planning rejects with a useful source location and launches nothing.
Validate the entire workflow; document explicit event, single Linux job, Bash, static env/defaults and sequential run-step limits.

stories.title: Bind plans to verified immutable snapshots
stories.value: run exactly the source I submitted
acceptance: Given a valid captured workflow, plan identity binds source/workflow digests and engine/capability versions.
Editing the checkout after capture does not change planned bytes.
Tampering, missing files, unsafe paths or unsupported manifest versions reject before acceptance.

stories.title: Implement supervised container execution for sequential Bash steps
stories.value: run a simple build in an identified environment
acceptance: Given a supported plan, ordered Bash steps execute in a separate attempt workspace using a digest-identified image.
Static environment precedence, shell/defaults and working directories have success and failure fixtures.
No ordinary job mounts host credentials or Docker socket; step events and bounded logs identify results and resources.

stories.title: Persist workflow submissions and per-step results in worker protocol
stories.value: disconnect and recover the same accepted run
acceptance: Given a retried identical submission key, exactly one run binds the snapshot and plan; changed input conflicts.
Attempt ownership persists before launch; disconnect/reconnect retains step results and evidence.
Setup errors, workflow failure and succeeded+0 remain distinct; existing development protocol tests still pass.

stories.title: Reconcile cancellation, timeouts, restart and disk budgets
stories.value: stop execution and recover without hidden work
acceptance: Cancellation and timeout escalation confirm owned-resource termination before a definitive terminal result.
Restart preserves queued work, never automatically repeats interrupted attempts, and blocks conflicts while cleanup is unresolved.
Disk-budget/full-disk fixtures reject unsafe new work and preserve active evidence.

stories.title: Establish M2 end-to-end execution evidence
stories.value: judge the first executable release against recorded evidence
acceptance: Public CLI fixtures cover success, nonzero failure, defaults, source isolation, cancellation and restart.
Evidence includes exact input/code digest, image, versions, terminal state, exit code and cleanup result.
Only succeeded+0 counts as success; local validation and GitHub reference comparison are labeled separately.

stories.title: Pin runner research sources and design conformance fixtures
stories.value: use traceable behavior references
acceptance: Record runner commit SHAs and primary citations for each source-derived claim.
Fixture specifications cover contexts, outcomes, job continue-on-error, output masking, command chunks and matrix exclude ambiguity.
Each expected result identifies documented, observed, inferred or unverified evidence; no external dispatch or upstream source import.

stories.title: Review parser subset and YAML dependency provenance
stories.value: choose a parser with understood semantics and obligations
acceptance: Compare maintained parser options with version, provenance and license evidence.
List scalar, duplicate-key, alias and bounded-parsing cases with expected accept/reject behavior for the proposed subset.
Deliver contract review first; review implementation when available and report blocking findings directly with precise evidence.

epics.title: Evaluate workflow conditions and exchange step data
epics.outcome: Authors can use conditions, contexts, step outputs and dependent jobs with explainable outcomes.
epics.exit_evidence: A supported fixture suite proves each semantic feature and explicitly lists unsupported cases.

stories.title: Evaluate expressions in the correct workflow context
stories.value: use conditions without phase-dependent surprises
acceptance: Own parser/evaluator handles a documented type/coercion/function subset without eval.
Each workflow key has a context/function availability policy and evaluation phase.
Positive, invalid-context, missing-property and type/coercion fixtures pass.

stories.title: Pass environment and outputs between steps
stories.value: consume data produced by earlier steps
acceptance: GITHUB_ENV, PATH and OUTPUT updates apply at the documented boundary; writing steps do not see later environment updates.
UTF-8, multiline, size limits and disallowed variable updates have tests.
Workflow command chunk boundaries and stop/resume behavior are validated; unsupported commands fail or are reported per documented policy.

stories.title: Report outcomes and evaluate failure conditions accurately
stories.value: handle failed steps without a false green run
acceptance: Persist outcome and conclusion separately around continue-on-error.
Status functions and condition defaults have success, failure, skipped and cancellation fixtures.
Job-level aggregation is implemented only against resolved evidence; unresolved behavior remains unsupported.

stories.title: Run selected jobs with their dependency closure
stories.value: execute dependent jobs in the right order
acceptance: needs graph validation rejects cycles and missing jobs.
Selecting a job includes required dependencies and immutable inputs.
Failure/skip propagation and job outputs match the declared contract with fixtures.

epics.title: Run checkout and reusable action steps
epics.outcome: Authors can run a checkout/setup/build workflow with owned action resolution and runtimes.
epics.exit_evidence: A pinned checkout plus setup plus build fixture completes with action provenance, lifecycle and cleanup evidence.

stories.title: Resolve actions to verified immutable content
stories.value: know which action code ran
acceptance: Resolve supported action references to immutable identities and record provenance.
Bound downloads, validate paths and metadata; reject unsupported or unsafe references.
Cache reuse verifies content; no act fallback or upstream engine import.

stories.title: Preserve submitted inputs through checkout and Git commands
stories.value: use checkout without replacing submitted changes
acceptance: Define and document checkout semantics for captured dirty/untracked inputs.
A pinned checkout fixture and Git-dependent build retain the identified snapshot contents.
No credential-bearing local Git configuration is copied; unsupported options reject explicitly.

stories.title: Execute JavaScript actions with setup and cleanup
stories.value: use supported setup actions
acceptance: Inputs, outputs and environment follow the declared action contract in a pinned Node runtime.
Supported pre/main/post lifecycle, reverse cleanup and failure behavior have fixtures.
Unsupported legacy runtimes/local pre behavior reject explicitly; runtime version and licenses are recorded.

stories.title: Execute local composite actions
stories.value: reuse a sequence of supported steps
acceptance: Composite inputs and nested supported steps evaluate in the proper context without invented INPUT variables.
Output mapping, working directories and shell requirements have fixtures.
Bound nesting and reject unsupported action types/features before execution.

epics.title: Expand workflow orchestration beyond sequential builds
epics.outcome: Teams can incrementally adopt more complex workflows without silent omissions.
epics.exit_evidence: Every enabled capability has bounded-resource and failure/cleanup fixtures plus a compatibility entry.

stories.title: Expand and schedule bounded job matrices
stories.value: test a declared set of configurations
acceptance: Implement include/exclude semantics against documented or observed GitHub evidence.
Bound expansion and max-parallel; deterministic child identities are recorded.
Fail-fast, cancellation and invalid matrix cases have fixtures.

stories.title: Call reusable workflows with typed inputs and outputs
stories.value: share tested workflow definitions
acceptance: Resolve supported workflow references immutably; validate typed inputs and outputs.
Detect recursion and bound nesting/dependency expansion.
Unsupported secret/permission propagation rejects; call-chain evidence is retained.

stories.title: Run Docker actions with owned cleanup
stories.value: use supported container actions
acceptance: Validate metadata, args/env and image/build provenance for the declared subset.
Persist owned resources before launch and clean them after success, failure and cancellation.
Host socket/credential access stays excluded; lifecycle and resource-limit fixtures pass.

stories.title: Run jobs with declared service containers
stories.value: test against a disposable dependency service
acceptance: Explicit service network and port policy prevents unintended exposure.
Readiness/timeout failures are distinguishable from job failures.
Success, cancellation and restart leave no unaccounted owned services.

epics.title: Make compatibility claims traceable and reproducible
epics.outcome: Maintainers and users can see exactly which behavior is supported and how it was validated.
epics.exit_evidence: Each advertised capability links to fixtures, source versions, local evidence and reference status.

stories.title: Catalog capability contracts and reference fixtures
stories.value: identify unsupported behavior before advertising it
acceptance: Create a machine-readable capability/fixture manifest with version and input identities.
Separate documented expectations, local results and observed GitHub comparisons.
Cover initial subset and retain unresolved research cases as explicit gaps.

stories.title: Compare local results with reference evidence
stories.value: detect semantic regressions
acceptance: Harness compares outcomes, outputs and ordering while ignoring incidental timestamps/log formatting.
Mismatch fixtures prove the comparator detects false success and wrong outputs.
External dispatch remains a separate authorized operation; missing references cannot report conformance.

stories.title: Explain supported behavior and local differences
stories.value: decide whether a workflow can run here
acceptance: Generate or verify compatibility documentation against the capability manifest.
Unsupported syntax has actionable diagnostics and fixture links.
Runner/image/action versions and intentional local differences accompany evidence.

epics.title: Give coding agents reliable execution tools
epics.outcome: Agents can submit, reconnect, inspect and cancel through the same contract as CLI users.
epics.exit_evidence: CLI and MCP agree on identifiers, outcomes, bounded logs and errors in end-to-end fixtures.

stories.title: Expose execution operations through MCP
stories.value: control runs without owning worker lifetime
acceptance: MCP maps describe/submit/get/list/logs/cancel to the existing protocol.
Disconnecting the adapter does not stop the worker or accepted work.
CLI and MCP observe identical run identities and final results.

stories.title: Recover from tool errors and reconnect safely
stories.value: distinguish retryable failures from run outcomes
acceptance: Malformed calls return structured tool errors without losing the connection.
Retry/reconnect preserves submission idempotency and cursor semantics.
Tests distinguish unavailable worker, unsupported capability, lost run and workflow failure.

stories.title: Retrieve bounded logs and artifact manifests
stories.value: inspect results without unbounded output or unsafe paths
acceptance: Paginate logs and manifests with stable run-scoped cursors and byte limits.
Artifact lookup confines paths to owned storage and reports missing/expired evidence.
Large-output and path-traversal fixtures pass through CLI and MCP.

epics.title: Let humans inspect and control local execution
epics.outcome: A developer can understand queue, results and recovery from a usable local dashboard.
epics.exit_evidence: Selected runnable design passes visible install-to-result, reconnect and cancellation scenarios.

stories.title: Compare runnable dashboard design options
stories.value: choose a usable execution view before implementation
acceptance: Provide runnable alternatives for queue, run detail and log navigation.
Show failure, lost, disconnected and unsupported-workflow states.
Record the selected direction before production UI implementation.

stories.title: Inspect runs, steps and evidence in the dashboard
stories.value: understand what ran and why it failed
acceptance: Implement the selected design using the public worker contract.
Show snapshot identity, status, steps and bounded log/evidence access.
Keyboard navigation, reconnect and large-output behavior have browser evidence.

stories.title: Cancel work and understand recovery in the dashboard
stories.value: stop a run without confusing uncertain cleanup with success
acceptance: Cancellation state reflects confirmed worker results.
Lost/cleanup-pending states explain what remains uncertain and allowed next actions.
Visible browser scenarios cover cancel races, disconnect and restart without optimistic success.

epics.title: Deliver an installable local preview
epics.outcome: A new user can install independently and complete the documented first workflow run.
epics.exit_evidence: P01-P12 acceptance passes from the packaged artifact and an external user completes the flow.

stories.title: Resolve distribution identity and third-party obligations
stories.value: distribute an artifact with explicit naming and licensing decisions
acceptance: Inventory runtime/bundled dependencies and their source/license/notice requirements.
Prepare owner decisions for project license and final public identifiers.
Record accepted decisions before distribution; ticket creation does not choose a license or authorize publication.

stories.title: Build a reproducible preview archive
stories.value: install outside the source checkout
acceptance: Archive includes version, checksums, dependencies and required notices for the supported platform.
Install and uninstall work in a clean disposable environment without internal coordination services.
Artifact build and exact digest are recorded; public publishing is a separate action.

stories.title: Diagnose prerequisites and follow a documented first run
stories.value: resolve setup problems without inspecting implementation
acceptance: Doctor reports versions, repository binding, Docker access and actionable missing prerequisites.
Document install, submit, follow, inspect, cancel, upgrade and removal.
Cold/warm startup, duration, peak memory and disk measurements are recorded without unsupported performance claims.

stories.title: Validate the packaged preview with an external user
stories.value: complete a real build using published instructions
acceptance: P01-P12 evidence names the exact artifact, platform, workflow input and terminal result.
CLI, MCP and dashboard results agree; external user completes install-to-result.
Record known limits and release decision; no publication is implied by test success.

epics.title: Discover private remote execution requirements
epics.outcome: Decide whether and how to extend local execution to authenticated private machines.
epics.exit_evidence: A reviewed proposal identifies trust boundaries, protocol/lifecycle changes, success criteria and a go/no-go decision.

stories.title: Specify remote identity, transport and attempt ownership
stories.value: understand the requirements for using a private remote worker
acceptance: Document auth, TLS, leases, input transfer, cancellation and disconnected outcomes.
Identify protocol changes and compatibility risks against local behavior.
Deliver a proposal and bounded experiment plan; no remote service deployment.

stories.title: Review the private remote execution proposal
stories.value: choose a separately scoped remote milestone
acceptance: Compare proposed design against lifecycle and threat-model requirements.
Record open risks, cost/operability questions and measurable experiment exits.
Record keep/defer/reject direction before creating implementation commitments.

epics.title: Discover isolation requirements for serving unrelated customers
epics.outcome: Decide whether a managed multi-customer service is viable as a separate product milestone.
epics.exit_evidence: A reviewed proposal separates tenant isolation, service operations and economics from local/remote worker scope.

stories.title: Assess tenant isolation and abuse boundaries
stories.value: understand requirements before hosting untrusted customer jobs
acceptance: Compare candidate isolation boundaries and secret/network/artifact separation.
Identify abuse, quotas, audit and incident-response requirements.
Document risks and experiment criteria without claiming local Docker isolation is sufficient.

stories.title: Evaluate managed service viability and decision gates
stories.value: decide whether managed execution should proceed
acceptance: Propose capacity, availability, billing and support responsibilities with assumptions.
Document experiments needed to validate cost and isolation claims.
Record a separate go/no-go decision; no customer serving or deployment is authorized by this backlog.
